of a building or plant must be considered as a whole, While water mist fire protection part, though an important one, of the available facilities, it should not be assumed that their removes the need to consider supplementary measures. such as the provision of portable mobile appliances for first aid or emergency use or measures to deal with special hazards.

Water mist systems have been found to be effective for the suppression or extinguishment of a wide variety of exposed and shielded Class B hydrocarbon pool tires and for combinations of incidental Class A and Class B fires. Water mist systems have also demonstrated their effectiveness on some Class A fires, including insulated electrical cable f~res. Ibis standard is not intended to be a substitute per~ormancc to water mist protection, for sprinkler systems, which provide similar or equivalent

Indian Standard WATER MIST FIRE PROTECTION SYSTEMS -- SYSTEM DESIGN, INSTALLATION AND COMMISSIONING -- CODE OF PRACTICE
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard lays down minimum requirements for design, installation and commissioning of water mist fire protection systems using potable water. 1.2 Sea water may be used in installations like ships. When sea water is used system shall be flushed after each application. 2 REFERENCES The standards listed at Annex A contain provisions which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid, All standards are subject to revision and parties to agreement based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards given at Annex A. 3 GENERAL 3.1 The standard is limited to systems that have demonstrated acceptable levels of performance in fire tests as part of a testing process. They may be arranged as total flooding, zoned or local application systems and designed for suppression or extinguishment, This standard establishes minimum requirements for water mist fire protection technology and is based on sound engineering principles, test data and field experience. Water mist systems are specialized fire protection systems. Design and installation of these systems requires specialized training, knowledge and experience, For systems using additives, of3 and 12 shall apply. the requirements 3.3 Classification 3.3.1 Low Pressure Based on Working W(zter Mist System piping is Pressure

A water mist system where the distribution subjected to pressure of 1.2 MPa or less. 3,3.2 lntermediote Pressure

Water Mist Systetn

A water mist system where the distribution piping is subjected to pressure greater than 1,2 MPa but less than 3.5 MPa, 3.3.3 High Pressure Water Mist System

A water mist system where the distribution piping is subjected to the pressure of 3.5 MPa or greater. 3.4 Classification Based on Type of Fuel

Overall fire hazard is directly related to the type and quantity of the fuel present in a space, The ease of ignition/reign ition of the fuel, the fire growth rate, and the difficulty of achieving control, suppression, extinguishment, or any combination thereof, shall be considered when selecting or designing a water mist system. 3.4.1 Class A Fires

Fuel loading and configuration shall be considered when selecting/designing a system to protect a space If fire or area containing Class A materials. extinguishment is desired, consideration shall be given to the potential for deep-seated fires as well as to the potential for smoldering fires. 3.4.2 Class B Fires

Water mist fire protection systems are herein referred to as a system or the system. 3.2 This standard addresses the use of fine water sprays for the efficient extinguishment of fires. Water mist systems may be effective on several classes of fire and various applications within those classes, provided they have been tested for the particular application and class. 1

The hazard associated with Class B fires is related primarily to the fuel loading, fuel configuration, flashpoint and burning rate of the fuel. Preburn time also affects the overall characteristics of the fire. Class B fires are grouped into two categories -- Two-dimensional pool tires and three-dimensional spray and t-arming fuel fires. rates, nozzle pressures and volumes and spray densities of water mist, These systems have the specific pipe sizes, maximum and minimum pipe lengths, flexible hose, number of fittings and number and types of nozzles ( .Yee Fig. 2 ). 3.10.2 En<yincered ,~\'s/eIJI

The drop size distribution of a spray does not uniquely define its suitability for a given application. It is inseparable from the spray direction relative to the fire plume, its velocity and flLIx density. The momentum of an element of spray is the product of its velocity ( which includes direction as well as speed ) and the mass of dispersed water droplets. Therefore, all three variables, that is, drop size distribution. flux density and momentum are involved in deter-mining the ability to extinguish a fire in a given scenario. Water mist systems offer potential benefits for many specialized applications, particularly when available water supplies are limited or when the application of water must be restricted. Potential benefits may also exist for applications previously protected by gaseous and other specialized fire suppressant system or extinguishing agents.

A water mist system where, as required by the accepting authority, individual calculation and design shall be done to determine the system flow rates, pipe sizes, area or volume protected by the system, discharge density of water mist, number and types of nozzles and nozzle placement. 3.10.3 De[I/<ye System

A water mist system using nozzles attached to a piping system that are connected to a water supply through a valve and where all nozzles discharge simultaneously ( .seti Fig. 3 ). 3.10.4
L@' ,yl's/en7

3.9 A water mist system is a fire protection system using very fine water sprays ( that is water mist ). The very small water droplets allow the water mist to suppress or extinguish fires by cooling the flame and fire plume. oxygen displacement by water vapour and radiant heat attenuation. Due to the presence of larger drops, higher mass !1OWrates are earlier to achieve with Class 2 sprays than with Class 1 sprays. The larger drops are not so large as to be ineffective on liquid fuel fires. However, con. sicierable surface wetting occurs with sprays in Ibis ratlge; therefore a Class 2 mist is also likely to be effective on fires involving ordinary combustibles. Class 3 water mists are typically generated by intermediate pressure, small orifice sprinklers, impingement nozzles of various sorts and fire hose fognozztes. 3.1 () System Types

A water mist system using sealed nozzles attached to a piping system containing air, nitrogen or inert gas under pressure, the release of which (as from an opening of sealed nozzle) allows the water sLipply pressure to open a dry-pipe valve. The water then flows into the piping system and out through any nozzles that have opened. 3.10.5 Prc'(lc[l(lll
L$J)SIC'lll

A water mist system using sealed nozzles attached to a piping system containing air that might or might not be under pressure, with a supplemental detection system installed in the same areas as the mist nozzles. The actuation of the detection system opens a valve and the water then flows into the piping system and out through any nozzles that have opened. 3.10.6 wet ,$yslem

A water mist system using sealed nozzles attached to a piping system containing water and connected to a water supply so that water discharges immediately from nozzles that are operated by the heat from a fire. 3.10.7 Tc][o[ Flooding ,Tystern water in an

A water mist distribution system is a system that is connected to a water supply and equipped with one or more nozzles capable of delivering water mist. 4.1 I Fire Control �� The limitation of the growth of a fire by pre-wetting adjacent combustibles and controlling ceiling gas temperatures to prevent structural damage. 4.12 Fire Extinguishment -- The complete suppression of a fire until there are no burning combustibles. 4.13 Fire Suppression --The sharp reduction of the rate of heat release ofa fire and the prevention of regrowth. 4.14 Manual -- Requiring accomplish a function, human intervention to

For the purpose of this standard, the definitions below shall apply.

given

4.1 Atomizing Media --- Compressed air or nitrogen that produce water mist by mechanical mixing with water. 4.2 Automatic -- Performing a function without the necessity of human intervention. 4.3 Containers -� A cylinder to store liquids or gases. or other vessel used

4.4 Container Discharge Valve --A valve directly connected to a container which, when actuated, releases extinguishing agent into the distribution piping. 4.5 Deep Seated Fire -- A deep seated fire become established beneath the surface of a fibrous or particulate material. This may result from flaming combustion at the surface or from ignition within the mass of the fuel. Smoldering combustion may then progress slowly through the mass. 4.6 Density -- System application rate, which may be expressed in the following two ways: a) Discharge density of the flow from the system in respect of the area of the risk and expressed as l/nlin/m J. Flux density of the flow from the system in respect of the volume of the risk and expressed, in l/min/m3.

4.15 Monitoring �� The supervision of the operating integrity of an electrical, mechanical, pneumatic or hydraulic control feature of a system. 4.16 Nominal Size ( DN) -- A numerical designation of size which is common to all components in a piping system other than components designated by outside diameters or by thread size. It is a convenient round number for reference purposes and is only loosely related to manufacturing dimensions. 4.17 Operating Device -- Any component involved between actuation and release of extinguishment. 4.18 Water Mist -- A water spray for which the DvqO as measured at the coarsest part of the spray in a plane 1 m from the nozzle, at its minimum design operating pressure. is less than I 000 ~m. 4.19 Water Mist Nozzle �-A special purpose device containing one or more orifices designed to produce and deliver water mist: a) Sealed nozzle -- A nozzle that operates independently of other nozzles by means of a detection and activation device built into the nozzle. Opetl no:zie � A nozzle that contains open orifices suitable to connect distribution pipe network to discharge the water or fluid flow through the pipe. H)dwid no~zle �- A nozzle that operates using a combination of the two methods in (a) and (b). A hybrid nozzle contains a built-in detection and activation device which can be activated by independent detection means.

b)

4.7 Directional Valve -- A device for controlling the passage of the extinguishing agent from a supply manifold, directing it to pre-selected area(s) of protection. 4.8 Distribution System -- All pipework and fittings downstream of any container valve, deluge valve or other control assembly. 4.9 DV~-- A drop diameter such that the cumulative volume, from zero diameter to this respective diameter, is the percentage of the corresponding sum of the total distribution. IS 15519:2004 6 SAFETY 6.1 Hazards REQUIREMENTS to Personnel 7 SYSTEM 7.1 General A system shall be designed and installed in accordance with its application for the specific hazards and performance objectives. Compliance with the above shall address compartment geometry, fire hazard, and system variables. 7.2 Enclosure Variables DESIGN

For fire situations, suitable safeguards shall be provided to ensure prompt evacuation of and to prevent entry into hazardous atmospheres and also to provide means for prompt rescue of any trapped personnel. Safety items such as personnel training, warning signs, discharge alarms, self-contained breathing apparatus, evacuation plans, and fire drills shall be considered. 6.2 Electrical Clearances

The clearance is the air distance between water mist system equipment, including piping and nozzles, and unenclosed or uninsulated ]ive electrical components at othcrthan ground potential. The minimum clearances provided are for the purpose of electrical clearance under normal conditions; they are not intended for use as safe distances during water mist system operation, 6.2.1 All system components shall be located to minimum clearances from unenclosed and uninsulated energized electrical components in accordance with

Floor area, enclosure volume, ceiling height, ventilation conditions and the like, shall be considered when designing a system in regard to nozzle location, system flow rate and the total water usage of the system. 7.3 Nozzles 7.3.1 Nozzles shall be installed in accordance with lmanufacturer's instructions. The minirnulm and maximum nozzle height limitations, nozzle spacing limitations, distance from walls, obstructions to nozzle discharge , distance below ceilings, spacing under pitched or curved surfaces shall be in accordance with manufacturer's instructions. 7.3.2 Nozzles subject to mechanical damage shall be protected with approved guards. Guards shall not significantly reduce the effectiveness of the nozzle. 7.3.3 Escutcheon plates used in a recessed or flush-type nozzle installation shall be a part of approved nozzle assembly. 7.3.4 Ordinary temperature-rated used unless otherwise specified. 7.4 Ventilation nozzles shall be

6.4 Water

6.4.1 Water mist system with additives protecting normally occupied areas shall incorporate a manual lock off valve unless the additive in the concentration used has been evaluated as safe for human exposure by an appropriate authority. The valve, lvbere fitted, shall be locked whenever the protected area is occupied, 6.4.2 Water mist systems using potable water or natural sea water are not considered to present a toxicological or physical hazard and are safe for use in occupied areas. 7

7.8 The water supply for a system can be either limited or unlimited and shall comply with the requirements of 9. 7.9 Components System components shall be suitable for the pressures and environment imposed on them and shall comply with the relevant Indian Standard or shall be listed as suitable for the intended application, and shall comply with 12. 7.10 Extinguishing Agent

The extinguishing agent, propellant or pressurizing gas and any other additives, shall be compatible with each other and the materials used in the construction of the system. 7.11 Additives Additives may be used in water mist systems to achieve a number of diverse objectives, including the following: a) b) c) d) 7.11.1 Improved ability, Application fire suppression or extinguishing

For certain systems a well-enclosed and sealed space is preferred. Particular attention should be given to openings around cables and duct entries into the space, return air louvers, and the like. 9 WATER 9.1 General Water supplies for system shall be either one or both of the following: a) Unlimited water supply -- through main connection, natural sea water suction line, reservoir or tank Limited water supply -- from stored pressure water container connected to external gas pressure supply. SUPPLIES

b)

of mist to water soluble fuels,

Protection of the system against fi-eezing, and Prevention Limitations of bacterial contamination.

Water supplies shall satisfy the maximum system demand at the approved rate of discharge for a period of not less than 10 min. 9.2 Unlimited Water Supply

The employment of additives in water mist systems imposes limitations. Any system incorporating an additive shall: a) b) be tested with that specific additive, additive concentration and its method of introduction; be clearly identified by means of container labels and warning signs as a system using additives; and be calculated by means other than IS 2952 ( Part 2 ) / 1S 4477 ( Part 2 ), unless it can be shown that the additive has negligible effect on the flow characteristics of water, such as density and viscosity. Systems

Unlimited water supply shall satisfy the maximum system demand at a listed rate for a period not less than 90 min. A filter or strainer shall be provided at each water The filter or strainer shall be supply connection. installed downstream of all piping that is not corrosion resistant. Such strainer shall be provided with a clean-out port %md shall be arranged to facilitate inspection, maintenance and replacement. Water supply pumps supplying water to mist system shall be of sufficient capacity to meet the system demand and requirements of the approval. Pumps, pump controls and valves shall be located as close as possible to the hazard or hazards they protect; however they shall be located outside the risk. 9.3 Limited Water Supply Except in the case of pre-engineered systems arranged for two complete discharges in accordance with their approval conditions, limited water supplies shall satisfy the maximum system demand 9

Regulators controlling the supply of water and atomizing gas shall be listed for the intended purpose. A check valve or other means shall be installed in the piping at the supply point to every nozzle to prevent the entrance of water into the atomizing gas. Filters or other means to protect nozzles from obstructions shall be provided. Where used, air compressors shall be a dedicated source and shall be listed for use on fire protection systems. Electrically driven compressors used as a dedicated supply shall be connected to the line side of the main switch. AND INSTALLATION

A reserve supply of water and atomizing or pressurizing gas shall be provided where the extinguishing agent can not otherwise be replaced within 24 h following system operation or if a single water suppiy is used for multiple risks. If a manual changeover is necessary, the mechanism shall be readily accessible from outside of the risk. Means shall be provided to prevent discharge of reserve supplies from open manifold connections when supplies are removed for servicing. The reserve quantities shall be identical to the initial supply. 10 PRESSURIZED ARRANGEMENT STORAGE CONTAINER

c)

d) e)

o

12 COMPONENTS 12.1 General

The arrangement of pressurized storage containers and accessories for either water or gas, shall be as follows: a) Containers and accessories shall be located and arranged so that inspection, testing, recharging and other maintenance are facilitated, and interruption to protection is kept to a minimum. Containers should be located outside of, and as near as practicable to, the risk. Containers protecting a single risk can be located within the protected area they serve only if sited to minimize the risk of exposure to fire and explosion. NOTE -- Storage temperature should not exceed 55�C nor be less than O"C, unless the system is designed for operation in storage temperatures
outside this range. External heating or cooling may be used to keep the temperature within the desired range.

System components including pipe, tube and fittings referred to in this clause shall be suitable for the pressures, temperatures and environment imposed on them. They shall comply with the relevant Indian Standard.
NOTE -- For the purpose of this standard pipe also implies tube.

b)

12.2 Valves 12.2.1 General

All valves on a system pipework utilizing stored pressure containers shall be rated at not less than the maximum container pressure at 55"C. 12.2.2 Isolating Valves

c)

Containers shall be so located that they are not subject to severe weather conditions or to mechanical, chemical or other damage. Where excessive climatic or mechanical exposures are expected, suitable guards or enclosures shall be provided. Reliable means shall be provided to indicate the pressure in refillable, pressurized gas containers. 10

There shall be no isolating valve between a container and the discharge nozzles other than the container discharge valve, directional valves, manual lock-off valves where fitted or valves required for flow testing. 12.2.3 Valve Monitoring

d)

Any normally closed or open valve in the waterway shall be monitored or locked in its operating position.

IS 15519:2004

12.2.4

Valve Protection

All installed valves shall be protected against mechanical, chemical or other damage. In addition, container discharge valves shall be protected against impact damage during transit. Protection may be provided by valve protection rings, transit caps, or by employing impact-resistant valves. 12.3 Pipework 12.3.1
All

requirements of relevant Indian Standard and filler materials used in brazing shall have a melting point in excess of 535"C. Welding or brazing fluid residue shall be removed prior to installation. 12.4 Installation 12.4.1 of Pipework of Pipe

Preparation

Piping

system pipe work shall be constructed of Class A pipe complying with relevant Indian Standard unless otherwise permitted. Installation piping downstream of the system strainer shall be of corrosion-resistant material such as copper, stainless steel or hot-dipped galvanized steel to relevant Indian Standard. 12.3.2 Flexible Connections

Each pipe or section of pipework shall be cleaned after preparation and before assembly. The pipework shall be free of particulate matter and oil residue before the installation of nozzles or discharge devices.
NOTE -- When installing pipework, care should be taken to avoid possible restrictions due to foreign matter, faulty fabrication or improper installation. Pipe ends should be reamed after cutting.

12.4.2

Pipe Supports

Flexible connections used anywhere in the system shall be deemed non-combustible when tested in accordance with relevant Indian Standard, and shall be rated for at least the maximum expected pressure at 65"C. 12.3.3 Pipe or Tube Bending

Piping shall be securely supported and allowance shall be made for thrust forces, expansion and contraction. [t shall be designed to withstand likely vibration and mechanical, chemical or other damage. Where there is the possibility of explosion, the piping shall be attached to supports that are least likely to be displaced. In all other respects hangers shall comply with the requirements of relevant Indian Standard. 12.4.3 Distance Between Supports

Bending of pipe or tube shall be permitted, provided bends are made without kinks, ripples, distortions, reductions in diameter, or any noticeable deviations from a round shape. The minimum radius of a bend shall be in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications. 12.3.4 Pipe Threads

The maximum distance between supports shall take into account the total mass of the pipe and contents. The distance between supports shall be in accordance with Table 1. 12.5 Drain Valves Where used, drain valves shall be fitted at the lowest points in the pipework of dry systems. 12.6 Dirt Traps Where a system employs thread sealing materials such as tape or has welded or brazed joints, dirt traps shall be provided. Dirt traps shall consist of a tee with a capped dirt-leg at least 50 mm long. 12.7 All system piping and fittings shall be installed so that the entire system can be drained. 12.8 Discharge 12.8.1 Corrosion Nozzles Protection

All threads used in system piping shall conform to the requirements of relevant Indian Standard. Joint sealing tape, compounds or thread lubricants, shall be applied only to the male thread. 12.3.5 Fittings

All fittings on system piping shall be suitable for Fittings the maximum subjected pressure. downstream of the strainer shall be of corrosionresistant material such as copper, stainless steel or hot-dipped galvanized steel to relevant Indian Standard. 12.3.6 Flanges shall conform Indian Standard. with the

PRVS shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations, PRVS shall be installed when the supply pressure is higher than the design operating pressure of the water mist system. PRVS shall be capable of providing a stable regulated output at the rated flow capacity and design setting, over the full range of input pressures that will be experienced over the course of the discharge period. Downstream pressure creep under no-flow conditions shall not exceed the lesser of the downstream components pressure rating or the pressure relief valve set point, if provided. Pressure set, point-adjusting mechanisms on the PRVS shall be tamper resistant and the adjustment shall be indicated by a permanent marking. A means to indicate evidence of tampering shall be provided. The PRVS set point shall be set by the manufacturer. Permanent markings shall indicate the inlet and outlet connections of the PRVS. 12.11 Check Valves valves shall be installed in the main feed near the control valves of both the water and pneumatic system piping of a twin fluid system, to prevent the backflow of water or atomizing fluid into the companion piping. A check valve shall be installed between the system and the point of permanent connection to a potable water supply. Check valves shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's listing.

12.8.2

Nozzle

Clogging

Where external clogging is likely, discharge nozzles shall be provided with frangible discs, blow-off caps or other suitable devices. These devices shall provide an unobstructed opening upon system operation and shall be arranged so they cannot injure personnel. 12.8.3 Spare Nozzles

12.12 Pressure Where sealed thermally activated nozzles are installed in a system, a stock of minimum 10 percent spare nozzles or thermal activators, shall be provided and housed in a suitable cabinet. 12.9 Strainers Line strainers or filters shall have a clean-out port preferably with replacement strainer or filter elements. Filters or strainers without replaceable elements may only be used if they are included as a component of a 1isted system. Such filters or strainers shall be installed with demountablejoints to facilitate the removal and replacement of the complete unit. The maximum filter or strainer mesh opening shall be 80 percent of the minimum nozzle waterway dimension. Strainers and 12 12.12.1 General

Indication

A pressure-indicating device shall be fitted to each pressurized water container or gas cylinder and shall indicate whether the container is charged to its nominal operating pressure or is undercharged or overcharged. The device shall be clearly visible and legible when the container is mounted in its service position unless the location of the pressure-indicating device is identified. The minimum range of the pressure indicator should be 1.5 times the working pressure of the system. The accuracy of the indicator shall be 10 percent of the nominal system working pressure.

All devices shall be located, installed and suitably protected so that they are not subject to mechanical, chemical or other damage which may impede their correct operation. 13.3 Control and Indicating Euipment Automatic electrically controlled extinguishing agent extinguishant discharge systems, shall incorporate control and indicating equipment complying with relevant Indian Standard. A system is solely designed for manual operation, the control and indicating euipment shall comply with the system listing. 13.4 Audible Alarms and Visible Warning Devices

12.13 Storage 12.13.1

Gas Cylinders b)

Gas cylinders used for the storage and transportation of gas at high pressures shall conform with the requirements of IS 7285 and IS 8198. 12.13.2 Pressurized Containers

Containers used for water storage that are normally pressurized, or that are pressurized when the system is activated, shall conform with the requirements of relevant Indian Standard. 12.13.3 Pump Suction Tanks

Where pump suction tanks are used as the water supply for a system, they shall be constructed from concrete or steel. 13 CONTROL 13.1 General Control and actuation systems shall be electrical; pneumatic, mechanical, or any combination of these. Such systems shall be either manual only or automatic with manual override in accordance with IS 15493. 13.2 Operating Devices SYSTEMS

13.5 Mechanical 13.5.1 Automatic

Operating devices, such as storage container discharge valves, isolation and discharge controls and ancillaries shall incorporate manual reset facilities. Operation of any container release device shall cause operation of all containers required for that particular risk. 13

Automatic mechanical release systems shall employ suitable means such as cables and where required, drop weights. The control cables shall be run within protective tubes with free-turning corner pulleys at all changes of direction.

in these parameters shall be substituted using the worst-case conditions. The listing of the system hardware shall be consistent with the intended system application. Tests shall be designed and conducted to stress the system in order to determine the working limits and parameters of the system and to incorporate adequate severity to minimize the effects of test parameter variations.

Manual mechanical release shall be protected from accidental operation. The release shall require a push or pull of not more than 110 N and a movement of not more than 150 mm, to ensure operation.
NOTE -- Where required, a warning sign complying shall be displayed. 13.6 13.6.1 Pneumatic Release

Any leakage during this period, which results in a loss of pressure in excess of 10 percent of the test pressure, shall be corrected. 14.7 When cold weather does not allow testing with water, an interim air test shall be conducted as given in 14.7.1. 14.7.1 Intermediate and High Pressure Systems

For dry and preaction systems, an air pressure leakage test at 40 psi ( 0.28 MPa ) shall be conducted for 24 h in addition to the standard hydrostatic test. Any leakage that results in a loss of pressure in excess of 1% psi ( 0.01 MPa ) during the 24 h shall be corrected. 14.8 Pneumatic Pressure Testing Warning

Where practicable, the maximum number of systems that are expected to operate in case of fire should be in full operation simultaneously when checking the adequacy and condition of the water supply. 15
